questions.prompt: Which syntax renders a component value into the page as text?
questions.explanation: Interpolation, {{ value }}, embeds a value into the template as a string.

questions.prompt: Why should you write [disabled]="isSaving()" instead of disabled="{{ isSaving() }}"?

options.text: Interpolation is slower than property binding
Property binding sets the real boolean DOM property; interpolation sets the property to the string "false", which still counts as true
The disabled attribute does not exist on buttons
There is no difference; both work identically

questions.explanation: Interpolation sets disabled to the string "false", and any non-empty string counts as true, so the button never re-enables. Property binding binds a real boolean.

questions.prompt: When must you use attribute binding ([attr.name]) instead of property binding?

options.text: Whenever the value is a string
When the attribute has no matching DOM property, such as colspan or most SVG attributes

questions.explanation: colspan and most SVG attributes have no DOM property, and binding to them directly is a compile error, so use [attr.*]. ARIA attributes can be bound directly since Angular 20, but [attr.aria-*] works in every version.

questions.prompt: Which statements about template expressions are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: They are evaluated against the component instance, not global scope
You can reference window, document, and console
Assignments are not allowed (outside event bindings)
You can use the new operator to construct objects

questions.explanation: Template expressions run against the component and forbid globals, new, assignments (outside events), and chained statements.

questions.prompt: What is the modern function that declares a two-way bindable signal input on a custom component (e.g. value = ____<number>(0))?
questions.explanation: model() creates an input that can be read and written and propagates changes back to the parent binding.

questions.prompt: Match each binding syntax to the data-flow direction it represents.
questions.explanation: Interpolation and property binding flow in; event binding flows out; two-way combines both.
